The one-sided limits agree, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></munder><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to 2} f(x) = 5</annotation></semantics></math>. Also <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(2) = 5</annotation></semantics></math>. prompts.title: Differentiable where two pieces meet
prompts.context: Let p(x)p(x)={x2x≤12x−1x>1= \begin{cases} x^2 & x \le 1 \\ 2x - 1 & x > 1 \end{cases}
prompts.prompt: Is pp differentiable at x=1x = 1? Justify your answer with limits.
checklist: Shows <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> is continuous at 1: both one-sided limits equal <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1 = p(1)</annotation></semantics></math>

Finds the left difference quotient limit: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>→</mo><msup><mn>0</mn><mo>−</mo></msup></mrow></munder><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>h</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>h</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{h \to 0^-} \frac{(1 + h)^2 - 1}{h}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>→</mo><msup><mn>0</mn><mo>−</mo></msup></mrow></munder><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \lim_{h \to 0^-} (2 + h)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2</annotation></semantics></math>

Finds the right one: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>→</mo><msup><mn>0</mn><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow></munder><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>h</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{h \to 0^+} \frac{2(1 + h) - 1 - 1}{h}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2</annotation></semantics></math>, and concludes <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p'(1) = 2</annotation></semantics></math>

earns.answer: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><msup><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo></msup></mrow></munder><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to 1^-} p(x) = 1</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><msup><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow></munder><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to 1^+} p(x)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2(1) - 1</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(1) = 1</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> is continuous at 1. From the left, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>→</mo><msup><mn>0</mn><mo>−</mo></msup></mrow></munder><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>h</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>h</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{h \to 0^-} \frac{(1 + h)^2 - 1}{h}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>→</mo><msup><mn>0</mn><mo>−</mo></msup></mrow></munder><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \lim_{h \to 0^-} (2 + h)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2</annotation></semantics></math>. From the right, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>→</mo><msup><mn>0</mn><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow></munder><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>h</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{h \to 0^+} \frac{\left(2(1 + h) - 1\right) - 1}{h}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>→</mo><msup><mn>0</mn><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow></munder><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>h</mi></mrow><mi>h</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \lim_{h \to 0^+} \frac{2h}{h}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2</annotation></semantics></math>. The one-sided limits of the difference quotient agree, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> is differentiable at 1 and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p'(1) = 2</annotation></semantics></math>.

misses.answer: The derivative of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^2</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2x</annotation></semantics></math>, which is 2 at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 1</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> is differentiable there.

Differentiability at a joining point needs the pieces to meet and the slopes from both sides to agree; with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2x + 1</annotation></semantics></math> as the right piece, this argument would still say yes, wrongly.

earns.answer: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></munder><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to 3} |x - 3|</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 0</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= f(3)</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> is continuous at 3. misses.answer: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>60</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3(4 + 7 + 9) = 60</annotation></semantics></math> liters, an underestimate because it is a left sum.

prompts.title: Separation with the initial condition
prompts.context: Consider dydx=2xy\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{2x}{y} with y(0)=3y(0) = 3.
prompts.prompt: Find the particular solution y=f(x)y = f(x) with f(0)=3f(0) = 3.
checklist: Separates: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y\,dy = 2x\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>, then antidifferentiates: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{y^2}{2} = x^2 + C</annotation></semantics></math>

Uses the initial condition right away: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>9</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{9}{2} = 0 + C</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>9</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C = \frac{9}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>

Solves with the positive root, since <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y(0) = 3 > 0</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = \sqrt{2x^2 + 9}</annotation></semantics></math>

earns.answer: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y\,dy = 2x\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{y^2}{2} = x^2 + C</annotation></semantics></math>. With <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y(0) = 3</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>9</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{9}{2} = C</annotation></semantics></math>. So <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y^2 = 2x^2 + 9</annotation></semantics></math>, and since <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y(0) > 0</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = \sqrt{2x^2 + 9}</annotation></semantics></math>.
earns.why: The constant appears when the antiderivatives are taken and is found from the initial condition before solving for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math>; the sign of the root is chosen from <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y(0)</annotation></semantics></math>.

misses.answer: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{y^2}{2} = x^2</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = \sqrt{2}\,x</annotation></semantics></math>, and adding <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C</annotation></semantics></math> with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y(0) = 3</annotation></semantics></math> gives <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = \sqrt{2}\,x + 3</annotation></semantics></math>.
misses.why: The constant must be added when you antidifferentiate, not after solving for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math>. Added at the end, it gives a function that does not solve the equation.

prompts.title: Average value, not average rate

Gets <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>840</mn><mn>12</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>70</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{840}{12} = 70</annotation></semantics></math> degrees Fahrenheit

The average value of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>12</mn></mfrac><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>12</mn></msubsup><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{12}\int_0^{12} T(t)\,dt</annotation></semantics></math>.

prompts.title: Total distance with a turn
prompts.context: A particle moves along a line with velocity v(t)=4−2tv(t) = 4 - 2t meters per second for 0≤t≤30 \le t \le 3.
prompts.prompt: Find the total distance the particle travels from t=0t = 0 to t=3t = 3. Show the work that leads to your answer.
checklist: Finds where <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v</annotation></semantics></math> changes sign: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 2</annotation></semantics></math>

Splits the integral there: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^2 (4 - 2t)\,dt</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 4</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_2^3 (4 - 2t)\,dt</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= -1</annotation></semantics></math>

Adds the sizes: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4 + 1 = 5</annotation></semantics></math> meters, which is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>3</mn></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^3 |v(t)|\,dt</annotation></semantics></math>

earns.answer: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v(t) = 0</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 2</annotation></semantics></math>, with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v > 0</annotation></semantics></math> before and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v < 0</annotation></semantics></math> after. Total distance <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>3</mn></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \int_0^3 |v(t)|\,dt</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \int_0^2 (4 - 2t)\,dt - \int_2^3 (4 - 2t)\,dt</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 4 - (-1)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 5</annotation></semantics></math> meters.

misses.answer: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>3</mn></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^3 (4 - 2t)\,dt</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">[</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">]</mo></mrow><mn>0</mn><mn>3</mn></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \left[4t - t^2\right]_0^3</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 3</annotation></semantics></math> meters.

prompts.title: Position from a known later time
prompts.context: A particle's position at t=2t = 2 is x(2)=5x(2) = 5, and ∫26v(t)dt=−7\int_2^6 v(t)\,dt = -7.
prompts.prompt: Find the position of the particle at t=6t = 6.
